skill.name: session-memory
skill.description: Stores and summarizes project session memory so AI assistants can resume prior work with recorded decisions, patterns, and handoff notes.
skill.summary: Keep project context, decisions, patterns, and session handoffs available across AI coding sessions.
skill.author: Chachamaru127

security_audit.summary: All static external command detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and fenced examples in SKILL.md. The high-entropy and system reconnaissance findings are also false positives, but the skill has a low privacy risk because it encourages persistent session memory files that may contain sensitive project context.

remediation.issue: Persistent memory files can accidentally retain secrets or private project details.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear redaction checklist before writing session logs, decisions, patterns, or context summaries.

remediation.issue: Local memory files may be committed if repository ignore rules are missing.
remediation.suggestion: Document that session-log.md, context.json, and .claude/state should be ignored by default unless reviewed for sharing.

remediation.issue: The optional stop-hook workflow can append summaries without a final human review.
remediation.suggestion: Require review or filtering before automatic session summaries are appended to memory files.

static_findings.snippet: このスキルは `.claude/memory/` に作業履歴を保存し、
あわせて、重要な情報は「どこに残すべきか」を明確にします(詳細: `docs/MEMORY_POLICY.md`)。
- 各エントリは **タイトル + タグ**(例: `#decision #db`)を付け、先頭に **Index** を置く
1. 重要な決定を `decisions.md` に記録
2. 新しいパターンを `patterns.md` に追加
3. ファイル生成を `session-log.md` に記録
- **自動保存**: `hooks/Stop` により、セッション終了時に `session-log.md` へ要約を自動追記する運用を推奨(未導入の場合は手動運用でOK)
- **Git方針**: `decisions.md`/`patterns.md`は共有推奨、`session-log.md`/`context.json`/`.claude/state/`はローカル
- "what did we do last time?", "continue from before"

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Session Records May Capture Sensitive Data
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs assistants to save session logs, decisions, patterns, and context files under .claude/memory. This is useful, but retained project history can expose secrets or private implementation details if users or hooks write sensitive content or commit local logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly describes persistent memory writes and an optional stop-hook append workflow. Confidence is moderate because the skill also warns not to record secrets and recommends keeping noisy local files out of Git.

content.user_title: Preserve Session Memory Across AI Work
content.value_statement: AI coding sessions often lose context between conversations. This skill records session history, decisions, patterns, and handoff notes so Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can resume work faster.
actual_capabilities: Defines a .claude/memory folder structure for session logs, decisions, patterns, and context summaries.
Provides trigger phrases for recalling prior work and continuing from previous sessions.
Recommends separating shared knowledge from local session details and temporary state.
Shows example formats for session summaries, technical decisions, reusable patterns, and project context.
Guides assistants to update memory at session start, during work, and at session end.
limitations: Does not include executable automation for creating or validating memory files.
Relies on the assistant and user to avoid storing secrets or sensitive information.
Does not synchronize memory across machines or remote services by itself.
Examples are focused on coding projects and may need changes for non-technical workflows.

use_cases.title: Resume Development Work
use_cases.description: Review prior tasks, unfinished items, and recent decisions before continuing implementation.

use_cases.title: Share Project Decisions
use_cases.description: Keep important architectural choices and reusable patterns in files that teammates can review.

use_cases.title: Maintain Assistant Context
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code concise project state without repeating background every session.

prompt_templates.title: Recall Last Session
prompt_templates.prompt: What did we do last time in this project? Summarize completed work, open tasks, and the best next step.

prompt_templates.title: Continue From Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue from the previous session. Read the memory notes, identify unfinished work, and confirm the next implementation task before editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Record A Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Add this decision to project memory with the reason, tradeoffs, related files, and tags: [describe the decision].

prompt_templates.title: Audit Memory Hygiene
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the project memory files for stale entries, duplicate notes, and sensitive information. Propose a concise cleanup plan before changing anything.

output_examples.input: What did we do last time?
output: Summary of the previous session with completed tasks and key decisions.
List of unfinished items that are ready for the next session.
Suggested next step based on the recorded handoff.

output_examples.input: Record the database decision for this project.
output: A short decision note with the selected option and reason.
Any follow-up work that should be tracked separately.

output_examples.input: Clean up session memory before sharing this repository.
output: Sensitive or local-only entries to remove or redact.
Shared decisions and patterns that are safe to keep.
A proposed split between team knowledge and local history.

best_practices: Keep decisions and reusable patterns concise, tagged, and easy to scan.
Review session logs before sharing or committing them to a repository.
Update handoff notes at the end of meaningful work sessions.
anti_patterns: Do not store API keys, credentials, customer data, or private messages in memory files.
Do not treat session logs as a complete source of truth for requirements or contracts.
Do not allow stale context to override current user instructions or repository state.

faq.question: What does this skill store?
faq.answer: It defines memory files for session logs, decisions, reusable patterns, and project context summaries.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill file is documentation for reading and writing memory notes, not executable command automation.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Should memory files be committed?
faq.answer: Shared decisions and reusable patterns may be committed after review. Local logs and context should usually stay private.

faq.question: How should sensitive information be handled?
faq.answer: Do not write secrets or private data into memory. Redact sensitive details before saving or sharing notes.

faq.question: Does it replace project documentation?
faq.answer: No. It supports continuity between sessions, while formal documentation remains the source for stable requirements.
